campaign.title: The Grand Blooming
campaign.subtitle: A living record of promises, discoveries, and consequences

entries.title: The Days of the First Steps
entries.summary: Seven days of ceremony, wonder, and uneasy promises at the Cradle of Blooming Light will begin the Blue Butterfly Cycle.
entries.body:
Feyrandralis has opened the Cradle of Blooming Light for a full week of lantern processions, garden salons, public trials of skill, midnight music, and the naming of a new Pilgrimage. Beneath the silk and flowers, Keepers are already arguing over why this cycle called adults instead of children—and why no council can explain the blue butterflies.

For seven days, the pilgrims may meet the city, learn one another's stories, make allies, collect rumors, and decide what kind of company they will become. On the final morning, they will take their ceremonial first steps together and choose which invitation becomes their first road.

The Festival Week

  1. Day One — Arrival: enter the Cradle and be recognized before the gathered city.
  2. Day Two — Names: register a name, a keepsake, and the road each pilgrim has left behind.
  3. Day Three — Voices: meet the newspapers, noble houses, Keepers, and petitioners competing to define the new cycle.
  4. Day Four — Hands: join the festival's contests and offer one act of service to Feyrandralis.
  5. Day Five — Shadows: face the first accusation of witchcraft before celebration turns to panic.
  6. Day Six — Promises: answer the invitations that will shape the Pilgrimage.
  7. Day Seven — First Steps: cross the living threshold and choose the party's road.

quest.rewards: Pilgrims' travel seals, the party's first chosen road, and a place in the living record

objectives.text: Day One — Arrive at the Cradle and witness the recognition ceremony
Day Two — Enter your names, keepsakes, and farewells in the living record
Day Three — Hear the factions and petitioners seeking the pilgrims' attention
Day Four — Take part in the festival and perform one act of service
Day Five — Resolve the accusation threatening the festival
Day Six — Consider the five invitations placed before the party
Day Seven — Complete the First Steps procession and choose the first road

entries.title: The Name Kaelport Forgot
entries.summary: Eleven letters ask the pilgrims to remember people whom Kaelport's families, ledgers, and servants insist never existed.
entries.body:
The sixth-night train from Kaelport arrives carrying eleven letters in eleven different envelopes, all written in the same hand: Please remember me. Each bears a legitimate household seal. Each household denies sending it. By morning, one of the petitioners' names has vanished from the passenger list.

The trail leads from Kaelport's rail terminus into its servant quarters, printing houses, and noble salons, where memory magic is treated as both inheritance and property.

The Road Ahead

  1. The Vanishing Ink: preserve the letters before their names disappear.
  2. The Houses of Many Voices: learn who profits when a life is edited out of polite memory.
  3. The Vault Beneath Kaelport: decide whether stolen memories should be restored, destroyed, or carried onward.

quest.rewards: A Kaelport archive writ, rail passage, and one recovered memory

objectives.text: Keep the eleven letters from erasing themselves
Follow the missing names into Kaelport's estates and archives
Decide the fate of the memory vault beneath the city

entries.title: The Morrowglass Promise
entries.summary: A Kaelport medical exhibition promises a perfect new body—but its first restored patient remembers three different lives.
entries.body:
The Morrowglass Anatomical Society invites the chosen pilgrims to witness the century's great triumph: a body rebuilt through anatomy, alchemy, machinery, and old magic. Hours before the unveiling, the patient wakes and names strangers as beloved family.

The Society needs discreet escorts, investigators, and witnesses. Its rivals call the work grave robbery. Its patrons call it immortality. The patient only asks which memories make a person real.

The Road Ahead

  1. The Exhibition: protect the patient when the demonstration becomes a public scandal.
  2. The Harbor Laboratories: trace the bodies, memories, and money used in the procedure.
  3. The Promise: choose whether the work should save the dying, be buried, or belong to no single patron.

quest.rewards: Access to restricted medical archives and the Society's restoration apparatus

objectives.text: Reach Kaelport and meet the restored patient
Discover whose bodies and memories made the restoration possible
Decide who may control the Morrowglass process

entries.title: The Seventh File
entries.summary: A sealed record from Saint Veyra's Rootward House rewrites a child's name every dawn, and every borrowed name belongs to someone missing.
entries.body:
A courier from Luthar's Gate arrives without insignia and asks the pilgrims to carry a locked intake file back to Saint Veyra's Rootward House. The document has named six different children in six days. None are in the House. All six are missing somewhere in Kaeltharion.

Tomorrow will reveal the seventh name. The Root Line wants the file surrendered, the Dusk Line wants it silenced, and frightened families have begun blaming witches and unplaced children.

The Road Ahead

  1. The Seventh Dawn: guard the file and learn its next name.
  2. The Root House: protect the children while searching records beneath the Grand Tree.
  3. The Old Root Gate: discover who is moving lives between worlds—and decide who is allowed to know.

quest.location: Luthar's Gate — Saint Veyra's Rootward House
quest.rewards: Root House sanctuary, sealed registry access, and the truth of the seventh name

objectives.text: Keep the changing file safe until the seventh dawn
Carry it to Saint Veyra's Rootward House
Find the people whose names have appeared in the file

entries.title: The Iron Pilgrimage
entries.summary: The Luthar-side pilgrimage road no longer remembers those who walk it, and a midnight train has arrived missing seven hours.
entries.body:
The Vigilant Order reports that the old route through Luthar's Gate has stopped accepting new ritual marks. The latest railcar crossed beneath the Grand Tree at sunset and emerged at dawn. Its clocks advanced seven hours. Its passengers did not.

The Gate Line has sealed the station. The Keepers insist the road must be restitched before the new Pilgrimage can safely leave the divided city. Both institutions want the chosen under their authority.

The Road Ahead

  1. The Lost Hours: question passengers and search the sealed midnight train.
  2. The Iron Gate: cross courts, patrols, and competing orders to reach the old road.
  3. The Living Stitch: renew the protection spell—or learn why the road has begun refusing it.

quest.giver: The Vigilant Order and the Cradle Keepers
quest.rewards: A Vigilant road writ, passage on the restored line, and authority to mark the first route

objectives.text: Investigate the passengers and midnight train that lost seven hours
Gain access to the sealed pilgrimage road beneath Luthar's Gate
Restore the living stitch—or discover why it rejected the old rite

entries.title: The Garden Behind the Silk
entries.summary: A plea sewn inside the festival's grand banner asks the pilgrims to find the true name of a child hidden inside Feyrandralis's patronage houses.
entries.body:
During the First Steps procession, a seam splits in the ceremonial banner. Inside is a child's message worked in blue thread: They gave me a beautiful name. Please find mine.

Feyrandralis has no orphanages. Its lost children disappear more gracefully—into apprenticeships, temple registries, servant contracts, and private patronage. The banner passed through six respected houses, and each denies knowing who stitched the plea.

The Road Ahead

  1. The Blue Thread: trace the banner through the festival workshops.
  2. The Patron Gardens: enter the beautiful houses where unwanted histories are kept out of sight.
  3. A Name Freely Chosen: decide what freedom, family, and protection should mean for the hidden children of Feyrandralis.

quest.giver: The Child with the Blue Thread
quest.rewards: The children's trust, a patron-house favor, and a true name returned

objectives.text: Trace the blue thread through the First Steps workshops
Learn which patron house hid the child who wrote the plea
Help the hidden children claim names and futures of their own choosing

entries.title: Historical Context: What Came Before
entries.summary: From the creation of Kaeltharion to the uneasy progress that preceded the Blue Butterfly Cycle.
entries.body:
Year 0: The New World Begins

After the Ancient Prison, the First Watchers helped create Kaeltharion from the souls who survived. They did not build a paradise. They built a chance. The world was made to be protected, not ruled. The earliest laws against godhood were born from this fear: that no being, no matter how loved, powerful, or wise, should ever be allowed to own the fate of all people again.

The First Centuries: Cities, Seeds, and Survival

The first settlements became cities. Magic was present, but not equal. Some people could hear the weave. Others could only live near it. The First Watchers helped shape the bones of civilization, but mankind was expected to grow without kneeling to gods.

The Pilgrimage System Forms

As Kaeltharion stabilized, the Pilgrimage became one of the world’s most important traditions. Chosen pilgrims walked sacred routes across the continents, carrying story, sacrifice, and magic with them. Their journeys helped renew the protection spell across the world. In time, this became ceremony. Then institution. Then politics.

Year 896: The Sky City of Auris Rises

Auris was lifted into the sky as a monument to achievement, power, and the terrifying beauty of mortal ambition. To some, it was proof that Kaeltharion could become anything. To others, it was the first sign that mankind had learned too much from the gods it claimed to reject.

The Long Middle Years

Kingdoms rose. Councils formed. The Vigilant Order expanded. Magical education became regulated in some regions and forbidden in others. The old pilgrimage roads became holy infrastructure. Entire towns lived and died by whether pilgrims passed through them.

The Late 1800s: The Age of Uneasy Progress

The decades before this campaign were marked by invention, urban expansion, class tension, and growing fear of uncontrolled magic. The world became faster. Messages traveled quicker. People moved farther from home. Secrets became harder to keep, yet easier to weaponize. Strange illnesses, missing persons, dream-plagues, false miracles, and unexplained magical incidents began appearing across several regions.

The Early 1900s: The Blue Butterfly Cycle Begins

For the first time in recorded memory, the chosen pilgrims are not children groomed for the role. They are adults, strangers, workers, nobles, criminals, lovers, widows, soldiers, teachers, runaways, artists, healers, liars, and lost souls. They were chosen at random—or at least, that is what the official record will say.

The truth is worse.

Someone’s story needed to be told. Someone’s path needed to change. Someone answered the plea.

entries.title: The Witch Problem
entries.summary: The word witch did not always mean monster, but in the 1900s fear needs a face.
entries.body:
The word witch did not always mean monster.

Once, it meant someone who touched magic differently. Someone who learned through hunger, grief, bargains, inheritance, blood, instinct, or need. Some witches healed. Some protected. Some stole. Some lied. Some saved people no one else would save.

But in the 1900s, fear needs a face.

Magic is becoming harder to explain. People are vanishing after making wishes. Children are waking with other people’s memories. Men and women accused of witchcraft are found with blue veins, blackened teeth, mirrored eyes, or no shadow at all. Entire towns claim a neighbor cursed their crops, spoiled their bloodline, stole their youth, or whispered to the dead through the walls.

The Vigilant Order insists control is necessary. Local churches without gods preach purity anyway. Courts begin accepting dream testimony. Newspapers print names before trials happen. Families turn on one another. Wealthy patrons hire private witch-finders. Poor communities suffer first, as they always do.

The coming decades will be remembered as the Witch Hunts.

You are standing at the beginning of them.

Not every witch is guilty. Not every hunter is wrong. Not every accusation is false. And not every monster looks like one.

entries.title: The Grand Tree and the Bloom Wardens
entries.summary: What the pilgrims know about the Grand Tree's caretakers, the lethal trials, and the lives used to sustain them.
entries.body:
What Has Been Witnessed

  • The Grand Tree of Blooming Light hosts the Days of First Steps and the beginning of the Pilgrimage.
  • The beings commonly called dryads administer its rites, remove its dead, guard its candidates, and enforce the tests. Quinn gives their proper name as Bloom Wardens.
  • The Writ's seed and altar channeled power into the Grand Tree. The twenty who died there were forcefully transmuted into flowers and new growth.
  • A living tree in the second test drew life, essence, and souls from twenty-three victims.
  • During the third-day test, Bloom Warden guards described dead teams simply as having failed.

Quinn's Account

Quinn says the Bloom Wardens are lost souls from earlier Pilgrimages whose stories were rejected. They stayed beneath the Grand Tree, grew into its caretakers, and now serve it: maintaining it, healing it when it is sick, and feeding it with failed pilgrims. Quinn's knowledge appears substantial, but this origin has not yet been confirmed by a second source.

What the Evidence Suggests

At least some rites convert people, possessions, emotion, or soul-energy into power connected to the Grand Tree. The party does not yet know whether this power renews the world's protection spell, serves another entity, sustains the Tree itself, or performs several purposes at once.

Open Questions

  • Did the former pilgrims choose to become Bloom Wardens?
  • What does it mean for a pilgrim's story to be rejected?
  • Why does the Grand Tree require sacrifice?
  • What is the Tree ultimately powering or protecting?
  • Do Cressella and every Bloom Warden share the same origin?

entries.title: Blue Butterflies and the Blue Butterfly Cycle
entries.summary: Impossible witnesses that choose pilgrims, open roads, reflect emotion, and leave blessings and harm in their wake.
entries.body:
Selection and Travel

Blue butterflies are not native to Kaeltharion. They appeared to the five before the Days of First Steps, accompanied a shared dream, led the chosen to trees, and opened portals to the Grand Tree. Cressella called the butterfly a witness to roads walked and refused—not merely a blessing.

Guides and Jailers

The butterflies opened the magically sealed rooms of the second test and guided the five into the soul-draining-tree chamber. Their ability to release the pilgrims did not mean the pilgrims were free to refuse the road that followed.

Emotion in the Third Test

Butterflies nested in the third-day reception chamber. As anger escalated, they changed from blue through purple to red, flew violently, struck the walls and one another, and began to die. When Azryn calmed himself, survivors returned to blue and settled back into the nest. The party believes emotional regulation was part of the test, but no Bloom Warden stated the rule.

Protection and Possible Illness

A magical hand could trap the butterflies but could not crush them because a protective effect intervened. A critically ill child fell asleep when butterflies passed his home and developed blue-flower markings. The timing is confirmed; deliberate causation is not.

Open Questions

  • Who sends or controls the butterflies?
  • Do they witness emotion, absorb it, judge it, or convert it into power?
  • Why can they open some wards while enforcing the logic of the trials?
  • Are the illnesses and blue marks a direct butterfly effect or a wider consequence of the cycle blooming?

entries.title: The Pilgrims' Codex and the Archive of Keepsakes
entries.summary: The living record that takes a name, a keepsake, and a farewell—and the preserved offerings of those who walked before.
entries.body:
The Rite

The Pilgrims' Codex is a vast living grimoire held in a blue blossom beneath the Grand Tree. Cressella described it as part of a pact with the road. It required each surviving pilgrim to provide three truths: a claimed name, a keepsake showing what they feared to lose, and a farewell naming what might not return.

The Codex was said not to judge, but to remember.

The Five Entries

  • Azryn Voss: a sapphire-set silver earring; farewell to Thalia for now, until the end of the road, spoken in Celestial.
  • Franklin Graves: his quarry warhammer; farewell to the weapon that protected him and gave him purpose.
  • Thalia Sova: a purple family-crest ribbon; farewell to the Luthar identity and the origins written around her.
  • Amara Mentivocis: her gold cape clasp; farewell to the memories she cannot remember.
  • Dagmar Ijs: one treasured earring; farewell to Rada.

The Archive

Thousands of letters, rings, ribbons, toys, seals, weapons, and other keepsakes from earlier Pilgrimages remain clean, labeled, and magically preserved in nearby chambers. The objects are tethered either to the chamber or to an entity the Bloom Wardens protect.

Open Questions

  • What does the Codex's pact permit or demand?
  • Can a name, keepsake, or farewell be reclaimed?
  • What purpose do the preserved offerings continue to serve?
  • Does the road treat each farewell as a promise, sacrifice, prediction, or instruction?

entries.title: Souls, Rebirth, and Rejected Stories
entries.summary: What the trials have revealed about consumed souls, rebirth, and the fate Quinn attributes to rejected pilgrims.
entries.body:
Soul Consumption

The second-test tree drew out life, essence, and souls. Destroying it stopped the flow. This proves that some threats beneath the Grand Tree can damage more than the body and may prevent an ordinary afterlife or rebirth.

Pebbles

Pebbles died while pinned to the tree, but his soul escaped consumption after the party destroyed it. The soul was expected to find another life. The party does not yet know whether a reborn person preserves identity, memory, or any recognizable mark.

Rejected Stories

Quinn describes Bloom Wardens as lost souls of former pilgrims whose stories were rejected. If true, failed pilgrims may face more than death: some may be retained, transformed, and assigned a new function beneath the Grand Tree.

What Is Not Yet Proven

The record does not establish that every dead pilgrim becomes a Bloom Warden, that Pebbles will remember this life, or that the Codex controls rebirth. These remain separate possibilities linked by the campaign's recurring treatment of souls as stories, records, and sources of power.

Open Questions

  • Who or what accepts or rejects a story?
  • Can a consumed soul be restored?
  • Can a Bloom Warden recover a former identity?
  • How does ordinary rebirth differ from the transformation beneath the Grand Tree?

entries.title: The Heartline and the Curated Pilgrimage
entries.summary: The world watches the Pilgrimage through a network of images, feelings, and messages—but it does not see everything.
entries.body:
What the Heartline Does

The Heartline is a world-spanning communication system known in major cities. It carries information, feelings, and images and is used to broadcast the Pilgrimage beyond the Grand Tree.

What the Public Saw

Sander said the world watched the group's first and second trials. His account revealed a crucial limit: viewers saw hours of the party sleeping but did not see the battle against the soul-draining tree. The broadcast is therefore selective, interrupted, censored, or otherwise controlled.

The Pilgrimage as Spectacle

Merchants sell trinkets bearing pilgrims' names. The public chooses favorites. Children learn the names and songs of earlier pilgrims and hope to be selected themselves. The sacred road functions simultaneously as civic myth, entertainment, commerce, and lethal institution.

Consequences

Isolde fears the broadcast may reveal her survival or location to enemies in Frostmarch. The extent of the Heartline's geographic detail is unknown.

Open Questions

  • Who chooses what the Heartline shows?
  • Can its images or emotional impressions be edited?
  • Do the Bloom Wardens, the Grand Tree, or another organization control the feed?
  • What did the public see during the mass deaths?

entries.title: Pilgrimage-Linked Illness and Blue Marks
entries.summary: A new magical sickness, sleeping children, uncontrolled magic, and blue-flower markings appearing around the cycle's blooming.
entries.body:
The Sleeping Child

An infant failed to wake for two days after blue butterflies passed over his home. He could not eat or drink, his face had begun to waste away, and something appeared to be draining his energy. A living-looking filigree of leaves and blooming blue flowers marked his left wrist.

Azryn detected magic resembling enchantment, but not a woven spell. His grimoire did not know the cause and called the effect itself harmless, despite the child's dangerous decline.

Known Pattern

Isolde recognized a newly emerging illness most common in infants unable to absorb magic. Adults appear more likely to survive it. No established cure is known, and the condition is associated with the blooming of a Pilgrim cycle.

Katrina's Sister

Before disappearing, Katrina's sister reported sickness, unusual dreams, spontaneous magic erupting from her hands, and small blue marks. Her final letter said she would undergo a scholar-led cleansing. Authorities later claimed there was no evidence she was missing.

Connections That Remain Unproven

The sleeping child and Katrina's sister share timing, magical disruption, and blue markings. The party has not proved that they have the same condition or that the butterflies deliberately caused either case.

Open Questions

  • What does it mean to be unable to absorb magic?
  • Where does the drained energy go?
  • What is the cleansing, and who performs it?
  • Are the blue marks symptoms, seals, roots, or signs of selection?
  • Can nourishment delay the illness long enough to find a cure?

entries.title: The Listener and the Living Record
entries.summary: Stories are being chosen, remembered, rejected, and watched—but the audiences may not all be the same.
entries.body:
Cressella's Listener

Amara read Cressella's thoughts after the Pilgrims' Codex closed. The Bloom Warden was excited by the stories this group might create and hoped—or prayed—that an unknown listener would hear them.

Stories as a Recurring Structure

The Codex records names, keepsakes, and farewells. Quinn says Bloom Wardens are former pilgrims whose stories were rejected. Sander believes pilgrims join the stories that hold the world together. The Heartline carries a selected version of those stories to a public audience.

Separate Audiences Until Proven Otherwise

The Heartline audience is real and identifiable as the watching public. Cressella's listener remains unknown. The record does not yet prove that the listener controls the Heartline, judges the pilgrims, rejects stories, or is the entity protected beneath the Grand Tree.

Open Questions

  • Who is Cressella addressing?
  • Who accepts or rejects a pilgrim's story?
  • Does the Pilgrims' Codex write for the listener?
  • Is the Heartline a public imitation of a deeper magical record?
  • Why did the five share a dream with the Man of Many Names before selection?

entries.title: The Natural Inquiry and Master Mordenkainen
entries.summary: Investigators who study changing Pilgrim cycles, inherited magic, unstable memory, ritual contamination, and the marks left by the Grand Tree.
entries.body:
Sarah's Visit

Sarah identified herself as a traveling archivist and magical-studies investigator from Draval's Natural Inquiry organization, acting under Master Mordenkainen. She carried institutional credentials and a seal bearing her master's magical signature.

Subjects of Interest

Sarah asked whether the Grand Tree spoke; whether its roots reacted to anger, fear, blood, or names; whether the pilgrims dreamed of doors, cages, insects, roots, or voices beneath the earth; and whether they believed they were chosen or that something chose through them. She also asked about unusual inheritance, unstable memory, ritual contamination, and forms of blooming.

Bloom Resonance

Using a winged, blue-lensed monocle, Sarah examined Amara and identified a form of resonance left by contact with the Grand Tree. The organization's exact technical term still needs confirmation.

Reasons for Caution

Quinn hid when Sarah arrived and repeatedly warned Azryn not to engage. Azryn said that Master Mordenkainen was someone they should neither upset nor attract. Sarah has questioned Thalia before, particularly after the princess returned from her kidnapping.

Open Questions

  • What does the organization already know about earlier cycles?
  • What can its lens detect or record?
  • What does Master Mordenkainen intend to do with the findings?
  • How is Katrina's missing sister connected to the organization and its cleansing?

entries.title: Session Notes: Read Them Here
entries.summary: All full session notes live in History. Open a session below for the complete recap, scenes, choices, combat, discoveries, items, and unresolved threads.
entries.body:
Where the Session Notes Live

History is the campaign's complete session record. Each numbered Session entry contains the full recap, major scenes, important characters, choices and consequences, combat, lore revealed, items gained or lost, and unresolved threads.

The Lore Library reorganizes recurring discoveries by topic so the campaign can be read like a wiki. Lore pages distinguish witnessed facts from named-source claims, party theories, and unanswered questions.

Use History when you want to remember what happened in order. Use Lore when you want to understand what the campaign currently knows about a subject.

entries.title: Session 1: The Days of the First Steps
entries.summary: One hundred pilgrims entered the Days of First Steps. After twenty died in the Writ and twenty-three more fell in the second test, fifty-seven remained: the five at the heart of this record and fifty-two others.
entries.body:
The Blue Butterfly Cycle · Session I

The Days of First Steps

July 31–August 1 · The Grand Tree of Blooming Light

✦ 🦋 ✦

Previously On…

Five strangers were marked by impossible blue butterflies and drawn from Frostmarch, Kaelport, Luthar’s Gate, and the road into the newest Pilgrim cycle.

At the Grand Tree of Blooming Light, one hundred pilgrims offered pieces of themselves to a radiant seed—and watched twenty chosen die beneath the smiles of silent dryads. While the festival carried on around the bloodstains, the survivors found evidence that death beneath the Tree was being remade into flowers.

That night, the rooms promised to the chosen became locked, windowless cells. A familiar voice announced the second test. Blue butterflies opened the doors and led the five into a hidden chamber where a living tree waited among twenty-three dead pilgrims.

Niles was among the dead. Then the tree moved.

❦ The Butterfly’s Call

On the eve of the festival, blue butterflies appeared to Isolde, Azryn, Frank, Amara Mentivocis, and Thalia Sova Luthar. Each dreamed of a smiling man who seemed to have known them long before they knew him. His message was simple: the first step was not the road, but the moment they understood that they had been chosen.

At dawn, the butterflies led them to trees and opened impossible doors through their trunks. One by one, the five crossed into the crater beneath the Grand Tree of Blooming Light, where exactly one hundred pilgrims, dryad caretakers, flower-strewn stalls, and the music of the Days of First Steps awaited them.

✦ The Writ of Passage

Cressella, head dryad and caretaker of the rite, welcomed the chosen. She named the blue butterfly a witness—not merely a blessing—and asked every candidate to surrender something to an opalescent orb. Each offering dissolved into golden dust, carrying some part of its giver into the road ahead.

PilgrimOffering
IsoldeA single ration
FrankHis favorite hand axe
AzrynOne gold piece
ThaliaAn ornate dagger bearing her family crest
AmaraTen gold pieces

Then twenty pilgrims began to die. They choked, screamed, and bled beneath the Grand Tree while the crowd stood frozen. Smiling dryads gathered their bodies and carried them into the roots. Blue spider lilies rose where their blood touched the earth—and the festival resumed with terrifying speed. Eighty pilgrims remained.

🦋 A Festival That Refused to Mourn

The survivors drank, danced, traded stories, read fortunes, investigated the altar, and began forming the first uneasy bonds of the cycle. Amid the celebration, they gathered several troubling truths:

  • Azryn’s grimoire named the opalescent orb a seed.
  • The altar acted as a magical conductor, carrying power from the seed into the Grand Tree.
  • The blue spider lilies were not naturally magical; the dead had been forcefully transmuted into new life.
  • Frank recognized the dragon-and-sword emblem of the House of the Dragons, stirring memories of the Vigilant Order.
  • Death during the trials appeared ordinary to the caretakers—and expected by many of the candidates.

Isolde continued reading fortunes. Azryn preserved one blue spider lily as evidence. Frank and Amara found unexpected ease in one another’s company. Thalia kept vigil in her own way. Around them, the Grand Tree drank deeply and the music continued.

✦ The Second Test

At sunset, the dryads gave every survivor a key. Each key opened a private room hidden inside a tree—but once the doors closed, the keys vanished. Beds, tables, and candles became the furnishings of locked, windowless cells. Neither force nor ordinary teleportation could overcome the wards.

A familiar voice whispered to Isolde: “Test number two has started.”

Blue butterflies rose from the floors, unlocked the doors, and guided the five into a chamber centered upon a living tree. Its branches moved. Its flowers showed teeth. A trail of blood led to twenty-three bodies, some lashed and others impaled, their wounds dusted with strange blue pollen.

Niles, the Kaelport merchant who had tried to confess his feelings to Amara only hours earlier, hung among them with a branch through his chest.

One hundred began. Twenty fell in the Writ. Twenty-three more died in the second test.

Fifty-seven pilgrims remained: these five and fifty-two others.

The earth shook. The tree growled. Initiative had not yet been called.

The Five This Record Follows

  • Isolde hid her identity, read the warnings in her cards, and followed the butterfly beyond the locked cell.
  • Azryn distrusted the official story, investigated the rite, and carried away a blood-born spider lily as evidence.
  • Frank met fear with openness, friendship, and a warhammer swung against an unbreakable door.
  • Thalia offered her family’s crest before the crowd and followed the familiar magic of the second test without looking back.
  • Amara met every horror with practiced composure—until the chamber placed Niles among the dead before her.

Names to Remember

  • Cressella: Head dryad who conducted the Writ and carried the seed into the Grand Tree.
  • Quinn: Azryn’s tressym companion, sharp-eyed and careful about what should be surrendered.
  • The Man of Many Names: The smiling dream figure who framed recognition as the true first step.
  • Niles: A Kaelport potato merchant and acquaintance of Amara, now found dead within the second test.
  • The Caretakers: Dryads who maintained the celebration, removed the dead, distributed the keys, and displayed no alarm.

Threads Carried Forward

  • Why did exactly twenty pilgrims die during the Writ?
  • What did each offering truly shape—or purchase?
  • What joins the seed, the altar, and the Grand Tree?
  • Why do the dryads treat death as part of the celebration?
  • Who is the Man of Many Names, and why did he choose these five adults?
  • Why were Niles and the other twenty-two victims already waiting inside the chamber?
  • What does the living tree demand from the fifty-seven who survived?

When the record opens again

The second test begins beneath the roots.

✦ 🦋 ✦

entries.title: Session 2: The Road Remembers
entries.summary: The five destroyed a soul-draining tree, entered their names, keepsakes, and farewells into the Pilgrims' Codex, and began trading truths as fifty-seven pilgrims remained.
entries.body:
The Blue Butterfly Cycle · Session II

The Road Remembers

August 13 · Beneath the Grand Tree of Blooming Light

✦ 🦋 ✦

Previously On…

One hundred pilgrims entered the Days of First Steps. Twenty died during the Writ of Passage. Twenty-three more fell in the second test, leaving fifty-seven: the five at the heart of this record and fifty-two others.

Blue butterflies opened the pilgrims' sealed rooms and led the five into a chamber of blood, blue pollen, and bodies. Niles hung among the dead. A gnome named Pebbles still clung to life with a root through his chest.

Then the tree opened its eyes.

✦ The Tree That Ate Souls

Pebbles died before the five could save him. Azryn's examination revealed something worse than the wounds: the roots were drawing out the victims' life, essence, and souls. The bodies were not simply feeding a tree. Something living beneath the Grand Tree was consuming everything they had been.

Frank answered first, burying his axe in the trunk and bringing every root in the chamber to life. The five fought together for the first time.

Azryn

Protected Isolde, revealed a black-flamed halo and feathered wings, then poured blue dragonfire down the trunk.

Thalia

Turned Isolde's spilled oil into a devastating blaze and fought through the roots despite her wounds.

Amara

Called on her innate magic and sent green missiles unerringly into the burning tree.

Frank

Raged through ash and lightning, endured the roots, and struck the trunk hard enough to make it shudder.

Isolde

Discovered healing in her own trembling hands and restored Frank without spell or incantation.

Azryn's blue fire broke the tree from within. The stolen essence stopped flowing. The bodies sank gently into the earth, and Pebbles's freed soul was left to find another life rather than be devoured.

🦋 What the Fire Revealed

Victory left the five alive, injured, and unable to pretend their powers were ordinary. Azryn's moon-bright eyes, dark wings, and halo were no illusion. Isolde's touch carried a healing grace she could not explain. Amara and Thalia drew magic from distinct, distant sources. For the first time, the group could see that each of them had arrived carrying something the others did not understand.

Amara confronted Azryn quietly. He gave her the name beneath the Wanderer: Azryn Voss. They agreed to trust one another so long as neither moved against the other. Thalia, meanwhile, found something painfully familiar in Azryn's silver eyes. When he later wrote in Celestial, recognition became harder to dismiss.

Azryn gave Thalia a healing potion. Where the dead tree had stood, a brilliant door appeared.

❦ The Pilgrims' Codex

The door opened into a chamber overflowing with blue butterflies and flowers. Cressella waited beside a vast open book cradled in an enormous blue blossom. When challenged about a test whose failure meant death, she answered with the logic of the caretakers: the tree agrees, the world agrees, and we agree.

The book was the Pilgrims' Codex—a living grimoire of the world and a pact written into the road. It required three truths from each pilgrim:

  • A name to tell the road who they claimed to be.
  • A keepsake to show what they feared to lose.
  • A farewell to name the part of life that might not return.

The Codex does not judge. The Codex remembers.

Name EnteredKeepsakeFarewell
Azryn VossA silver earring set with sapphireA farewell spoken in Celestial to Thalia—for now, until the end of the road
Franklin GravesThe warhammer he had carried since the quarryTo the hammer that protected him and gave him purpose
Thalia SovaA purple hair ribbon bearing her family crestTo the Luthar identity and the origins written around her
Amara MentivocisThe golden Mentivocis clasp from her capeTo the memories she cannot remember
Dagmar IjsOne of a treasured pair of earringsTo Rada

Beyond the Codex lay thousands of earlier offerings: letters, rings, ribbons, toys, seals, and broken weapons, each labeled with a pilgrim's name. They remained pristine and magically tethered to the chamber—or to whatever the dryads were truly protecting.

Cressella closed the Codex and counted the survivors.

Fifty-seven pilgrims remained.

Tomorrow, the trials would begin anew.

✦ Stories for Someone Listening

Amara reached into Cressella's thoughts. Beneath the dryad's calm hospitality was excitement: this group would make wonderful stories. Cressella hoped—and seemed to pray—that someone would listen.

Amara shared the discovery with the others. The five might be pilgrims, sacrifices, or living entries in a record meant for an audience they had not yet met. Azryn's answer was immediate: before the next test, they needed to speak with Quinn.

The First Truths

Instead of leaving as strangers, the five stopped among the old keepsakes and tried—awkwardly, suspiciously, and sincerely—to become a party.

  • Amara named the Mentivocis gift for mental magic and admitted that she reads thoughts to judge danger, even when others call the act intrusive.
  • Frank revealed that he has been alive for only ten years, a fact that raised more questions about the body and history he carries.
  • Thalia admitted that she was abducted and cannot remember much of her past. She had expected good deeds from the Pilgrimage, not a trail of deaths.
  • Isolde explained that spirits sometimes speak through her tarot. She also revealed that she was once a Lady of Frostmarch, is no longer welcome there, and fears what will happen if she is taken back.
  • Azryn offered no simple history, but he gave the party his name, exposed the power he had been hiding, and promised Isolde that he would protect her.

The Cards on the Table

The Magician promised a life-changing journey and the possibility of success—but only if the five learned to work together.

The World spoke of a journey coming full circle and of finding what they sought within the group itself. Three other cards remained unspoken.

Names to Remember

  • Pebbles: A gnome who died in the second-test chamber. The tree failed to consume his soul.
  • Cressella: Caretaker of the rites and keeper of the Pilgrims' Codex.
  • The Pilgrims' Codex: A living pact that records names, keepsakes, farewells, and the road ahead.
  • The Listener: The unknown presence for whom Cressella hopes the pilgrims' stories will be told.
  • Quinn: The tressym Azryn believes may understand what the dryads are serving.

Threads Carried Forward

  • Who is listening to the stories recorded by the dryads?
  • What will the Codex's pact demand from the names written inside it?
  • Why are thousands of keepsakes preserved and tethered beneath the Grand Tree?
  • What part of each pilgrim's identity did the Codex recognize in their farewell?
  • Why did Thalia recognize Azryn's eyes, language, and handwriting?
  • What does Quinn know about the tests, the Codex, or the unseen listener?
  • Will the other fifty-two survivors face the same road—or entirely different trials?
  • What begins when Cressella calls the fifty-seven back tomorrow?

When the record opens again

The road already knows their names. Now it will learn what those names are willing to become.

✦ 🦋 ✦

entries.title: Session 3: The World Was Watching
entries.summary: On Day Three, the five heard petitions inside a warded chamber, learned that the Heartline broadcasts a curated Pilgrimage, and survived as four other teams died.
entries.body:
The Blue Butterfly Cycle · Session III

The World Was Watching

August 27 · Day Three of the Days of First Steps

✦ 🦋 ✦

Quick Recap

On the third day, the five were confined to a reception chamber and told to answer whoever came knocking. Quinn named the caretakers Bloom Wardens and claimed they were rejected pilgrims' lost souls, grown into servants of the Grand Tree.

A desperate mother brought a magically sleeping child. A merchant tried to sell the party's names. Sander revealed that the world watches through the Heartline. Katrina left letters from a missing sister, and Sarah of the Natural Inquiry arrived asking dangerous questions.

When the barrier fell, twenty more pilgrims were dead. Thirty-seven remained, and Day Three had only reached noon.

✦ Morning in the Reception Chamber

The festival regarded the survivors differently after two lethal tests. People recognized them and waited for a chance to approach. Bloom Wardens assigned the five a comfortable chamber overlooking Feyrandralis and gave them one instruction: remain there and answer whoever knocked. This was the day's test.

Before the first petitioner arrived, the party exchanged more truths. Thalia admitted that Azryn resembles someone from her past—an early attachment who betrayed her—and privately suspected she knew who he was despite his existence on another plane. Amara resolved to embrace her place as heir to House Mentivocis, diplomatic traders in knowledge and secrets.

Isolde asked Thalia and Amara to help find her husband, Peter, without revealing Isolde's survival to Frostmarch. Peter fell from a mountain while they fled her family, but Isolde believes he survived. She described caramel-dark skin, bright white hair, very dark eyes, and an unkempt appearance, and offered the Siren as the name to use in discreet inquiries.

❦ Quinn's Account of the Bloom Wardens

Quinn corrected the common name dryad: the caretakers are Bloom Wardens. According to her, they are lost souls from earlier Pilgrimages whose stories were rejected. They remained, grew into the Tree's caretakers, and now serve it—maintaining it, healing it, and accepting failed pilgrims as sacrifices and power sources.

Quinn described herself as researching a Pilgrimage from the front lines. She also warned Azryn that a red, horned woman had been watching him. Neither the watcher's identity nor Quinn's complete purpose was revealed.

The Cards Before the Door

Isolde read Thalia's past, present, and future:

  • Queen of Cups: past love and safety carried manipulation, secrecy, or a hidden price.
  • Nine of Wands: present resilience is becoming constant vigilance; carrying others while hiding the truth may exhaust her.
  • Nine of Swords: the future path she believes she must follow may produce anxiety, self-conflict, and a life she cannot accept.

Thalia dismissed the reading aloud, but its questions of duty and identity remained.

The Sleeping Child

The first petitioner was a mother carrying a son who had not awakened, eaten, or drunk in two days—ever since blue butterflies passed over their home. The child was wasting away as if his energy were being absorbed. A living filigree of leaves and blooming blue flowers circled his wrist.

Azryn detected enchantment-like magic that was not a woven spell. His grimoire did not know the cause and called the effect itself harmless. Isolde recognized a newly emerging illness associated with the blooming of a Pilgrim cycle, most dangerous in infants unable to absorb magic. No cure was known.

Azryn gave the mother ten nourishing berries to mash and feed the child. The party promised to seek an answer, but the child left critically ill. Afterward, Azryn trapped three blue butterflies with a magical hand; a protective effect prevented him from crushing them.

Names for Sale, Deaths Next Door

A red flash and a scream came from a neighboring chamber. Soon afterward, a trinket merchant asked permission to sell illusion-script souvenirs bearing the party's names. He described public favorites, fandom, and a market built around the Pilgrimage. The group refused.

Frank detained the merchant while the group demanded information. Two powerful Bloom Warden guards intervened and stated that the nearby team had failed. The merchant departed after giving Frank a small Pilgrimage trinket. The guards later delivered four bottles of Violet Lightning after the party requested alcohol.

🦋 Sander and the Heartline

Sander, a teenage admirer, wanted to meet the pilgrims and receive a blessing so he might be chosen in a future cycle. He called pilgrims stars, architects of wonder, and participants in the stories that hold the world together. He also repeated the public belief that the Luthar line descends from the world's first pilgrims.

Sander revealed the Heartline: a world-spanning system that carries messages, feelings, and images and broadcasts the Pilgrimage to major cities. The broadcast is curated. Sander saw the group sleep for hours but did not see their battle against the soul-draining tree.

Isolde panicked at the thought that Frostmarch might now know where she was. The Bloom Warden guards confirmed that no pilgrim could leave before dismissal. Azryn put Sander to sleep, disguised himself as the boy, and tested the exit. A magical barrier recognized him, froze him at the threshold, injured him, disrupted the disguise, and forced him back. Sander later left unharmed, believing Frank had blessed him.

The Butterflies Turn Red

A confrontation over Isolde's secrets made the chamber's table change color. Butterflies erupted from their nest, shifted from blue through purple to red, flew violently, struck the room and one another, and began dying.

Azryn deliberately intensified his anger to test the link. The light matched the red flash he and Amara had seen before the neighboring scream. When he slowed his breathing and calmed himself, the surviving butterflies returned to blue and settled. Approximately thirty had died, leaving the nest about two-thirds full.

The party inferred that emotional regulation was part of the test and that another group's escalating emotions may have caused its failure. No caretaker stated the official rule.

Katrina's Letters

Katrina, a woman associated with Draval, asked the party to find her missing sister. The sister's letters stopped two or three months earlier. Before disappearing she reported sickness, strange dreams, uncontrolled magic erupting from her hands, and small blue marks. Her last letter said she was going to a scholar-led cleansing. Authorities insisted there was no evidence she was missing.

Katrina had entered without authorization while attached to an envoy. She left the letters with the party and asked them to meet her later at a Feyrandralis tavern if they accepted the investigation.

Sarah and the Natural Inquiry

The next visitor was Sarah, a traveling archivist and magical-studies investigator from Draval's Natural Inquiry organization under Master Mordenkainen. She arrived with three guards. One looked exactly like Katrina, silently acknowledged the party, and urged them to conceal the letters.

Quinn hid and warned Azryn not to engage. Sarah presented her interview as voluntary and asked whether the Tree spoke; whether its roots reacted to anger, fear, blood, or names; whether the pilgrims dreamed of doors, cages, insects, roots, or voices beneath the earth; whether they were chosen or something chose through them; and whether their families carried unusual inheritance, unstable memory, ritual contamination, or forms of blooming.

Amara admitted only that the tree sought nutrients from failed pilgrims. Sarah used a winged blue-lensed monocle and identified a form of Bloom resonance in Amara after her interaction with the Tree. She produced credentials bearing Master Mordenkainen's magical signature and promised to return later.

What the Five Chose

  • They helped the sleeping child with nourishment and a promise, but could not cure him.
  • They refused to turn their names into merchandise.
  • They challenged their confinement and tested the exit ward.
  • They discovered and deliberately tested the butterflies' response to emotion.
  • They retained Katrina's letters as evidence and considered meeting her later.
  • They withheld most of their knowledge from Sarah and tried not to attract Master Mordenkainen's attention.

No formal combat occurred. The dangers were coercion, magical confinement, emotional escalation, institutional scrutiny, and the unseen deaths of other teams.

Items and Evidence

  • Katrina's letters: correspondence from her missing sister and the lead connecting blue marks, uncontrolled magic, and the cleansing.
  • Four bottles of Violet Lightning: delivered by the Bloom Warden guards.
  • Small Pilgrimage trinket: given to Frank by the merchant.

Threads Carried Forward

  • Are Bloom Wardens truly rejected pilgrims, and did they choose their fate?
  • What is the Tree powering with pilgrim lives, emotions, essence, and souls?
  • Who controls the Heartline broadcast, and what does it hide?
  • Has Frostmarch learned Isolde's location?
  • Where is Peter?
  • What is the child's illness, and is it connected to Katrina's sister?
  • What is the cleansing, and why did Katrina's sister disappear?
  • Why did one of Sarah's guards look exactly like Katrina?
  • What does the Natural Inquiry want from this cycle?
  • Who is the red, horned woman watching Azryn?
  • Who does Thalia believe Azryn once was?
  • What was the third test's actual rule?

Previously On…

A sleeping child bore blue flowers. The Heartline showed the world a story someone else had edited. Anger turned butterflies red, four teams died, and an investigator arrived asking about every secret the five were trying to keep.

Thirty-seven remained. The doors opened. Day Three continued.
